solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Make a trade, having put feet up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: paws are an animal's feet

explanation.surface: Someone does a deal after kicking back with their feet on the desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PAWS in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange one thing for another is to make a trade, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Little sister acquires strange power

indicators.note: the sister takes on the other word, so it ends up held within her letters

parts.note: sis is the short, little form of sister
something strange is new, unfamiliar

explanation.surface: A younger sibling suddenly gains a weird superpower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' reads as an anagram signal, but here it simply means novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscular strength or force is often called sinews, figuratively meaning power.

clue.text: Capital's new DJ with a funny name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: funny here means odd or peculiar, so the letters are put in a peculiar order

explanation.surface: A city has a new disc jockey who goes by an amusing name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges NAME into MENA.
explanation.definitionFit: N'Djamena is the capital city of Chad, in central Africa.

clue.text: Mother replants liberally in extensive plot

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: done liberally, freely and without constraint, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Mum is generous with her gardening, re-planting the large vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberally' rearranges REPLANTS into STERPLAN. 'plot' looks like a garden bed but means a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand overall scheme covering everything is a large-scale plot or plan.

clue.text: No longer 26, editor follows beer with short measure of Scotch inside

definitions.note: 26 across is CLEAN-SHAVEN; one no longer so has grown whiskers

indicators.note: the editor comes after the rest in the answer
the trimmed drink is placed inside the beer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a measure of Scotch is a whisky

explanation.surface: An editor has a beer chased with a nip of Scotch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to 26 across: the two answers are opposites, bearded against smooth-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bearded, with whiskers, is plainly no longer smooth-faced.

clue.text: Reportedly accept 50 in wages for secondary activity

indicators.note: signals that the word for accept is to be heard, not written

parts.note: to buy an idea is to accept it

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the word for wages

parts.note: pay means wages
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone apparently takes fifty on top of their pay as a side job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' applies only to the word for accept; the wages part is written normally.
explanation.definitionFit: By-play is subsidiary action going on beside the main action, especially on stage.

clue.text: Up all weekend, go about penning book

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as sheep in a pen, so one letter sits within the rest
about here means around and astir, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A sleepless weekend spent going about writing a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ALL WEEKEND GO, and 'penning' puts B inside. 'Up' looks like 'awake' but means well-informed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up on a subject is to be well informed, versed in it.

clue.text: Check flower and return

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
the carnation is a garden flower

explanation.surface: Inspect a bloom and then come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebirth of a soul in a new body is a return to life, so the sense matches.

clue.text: 50% off Mac company's software

indicators.note: half the name is knocked off, like a sale discount, leaving its front

parts.note: Apple is the company that makes the Mac computer

explanation.surface: A sale offering half-price Apple programs.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% off' removes the end of APPLE, leaving its front part.
explanation.definitionFit: An application program for a phone or computer is a piece of software.

clue.text: Average fellow makes excuse

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: An ordinary man comes up with an excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse an offence is to forgive it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Nobleman about to eat very soft Italian sausage

indicators.note: the nobleman takes the other piece into his mouth, so it goes inside

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A lord is about to tuck into a tender Italian sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to eat' looks like one phrase; 'about' is ON and 'to eat' puts PP in PEER. 'Italian' gives I, so the definition is only 'sausage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy dried salami-type sausage.

clue.text: Perhaps lead's about to be detected in a hill

indicators.note: the letter is found sitting within the other pieces

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill
C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A trail of lead ore is about to be discovered within a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads like the metal but is the leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead is the principal performer in a play, one example of a performer.

clue.text: Being excited in lively party? Not at first

indicators.note: the word goes without its opening letter

parts.note: a carousal is a drunken, lively party

explanation.surface: Getting thrilled at a rowdy party, though not at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being stirred up or stimulated is excitement, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Not working — perhaps playing golf endlessly around Britain

indicators.note: the shortened phrase surrounds the letter
the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: a golfer is on the links, a golf course by the sea; perhaps because that is one example of the phrase

explanation.surface: Not working, maybe just out on the course all day around Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is on the blink is faulty and failing, an informal idiom.

clue.text: She sings about the origin of Europa, a lover of Zeus for so long

indicators.note: the singer's name goes around the letter

parts.note: Cher is a famous female singer

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Io was one of the lovers of Zeus in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A singer performs about Europa, one of Zeus's loves, for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for so long' reads as a time span; 'for' is a link and 'so long' means goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British farewells, ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Some characters buried in earth under ballroom in film

indicators.note: some of the letters of the following words lie within them

explanation.surface: Something lies buried in the soil beneath a dance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderball is a 1965 James Bond film.

clue.text: Wild centaur swallows daughter — one might in 5D

definitions.note: 5 down is BY-PLAY; a performer in a side action might play it down

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the other one inside
wild suggests running out of control, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A savage half-horse gulps down a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges CENTAUR, which 'swallows' D.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor in background stage business might play the part with restraint, deliberately understating it.

clue.text: Drunk is very exhausted

parts.note: so can mean very, as in so tired
something used up is exhausted

explanation.surface: A drunk is utterly worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Soused is slang for heavily intoxicated, as if soaked in alcohol.

clue.text: Dried fruit is protected in downpour

indicators.note: the small word is sheltered within the other

parts.note: a downpour is heavy rain

explanation.surface: The dried fruit is kept safe during the storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a grape that has been dried.

clue.text: Devour nuts with ecstasy — outstanding

indicators.note: the drug's letter is added alongside, after the rest
nuts means crazy, so the letters go haywire

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Wolf down some nuts while high, a long-awaited treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges DEVOUR into OVERDU; 'nuts' looks like food to be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill still unpaid past its date is outstanding, a synonym for late.

clue.text: Teetotal group seen around student bar, one in European country

indicators.note: the group's letters are placed on either side of the rest

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a group of people who abstain from drink
L is for learner, a student driver
to ban is to bar
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Abstainers gather round a student bar in a European land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb meaning prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a Balkan nation on the Adriatic, in southeastern Europe.

clue.text: Shoot upsetting advert around hospital with religious figure

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant

indicators.note: the reversed letters go around the other
in a down light, upsetting turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Fire at an offensive ad about a hospital featuring a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns AD into DA, which goes 'around' H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buddha, Siddhartha Gautama, founded Buddhism and is revered as a spiritual teacher.

clue.text: Fly getting large, utilising the sun's energy

indicators.note: the word for fly takes in, gets, the letter within it

parts.note: to soar is to fly high

explanation.surface: An insect grows big on sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' reads like the insect but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar power is drawn from sunlight, so the word describes anything run on it.

clue.text: A lack of vision shown as lawyer sends in criminal

parts.note: BL, Bachelor of Law, is a lawyer's degree

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A short-sighted attorney has a crook brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges SENDS IN into INDNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to see is the condition of having no sight at all.

clue.text: New version reportedly resent

indicators.note: signals that the two letters are said aloud to give the word

parts.note: N for new and V for version, abbreviations

explanation.surface: A fresh edition is said to cause bad feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, the letters N and V give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge another's good fortune is to covet it, a near-synonym of resent.

clue.text: Wear Scottish flower

definitions.meaning: flower is crosswordese for river, something that flows

explanation.surface: Put on a Scottish bloom, like a thistle in a buttonhole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a bloom but is a river; the Wear is also an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: To put clothing on is one sense; the other is a river in northeast Scotland.

clue.text: No longer 5A, Charlie's consuming spare port

definitions.note: 5 across is BEWHISKERED; one no longer so has shaved off the whiskers

indicators.note: the letters take the other word into themselves

parts.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet, plus the S of the 's
spare means lean, thin
a haven is a harbour, a port

explanation.surface: Charlie eats while the port is to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer and 5 across are opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: A face freshly shaved has lost all its whiskers.
